topic.question: How bridges carry heavy loads
topic.title_suggestion: How Bridges Carry Heavy Loads? Facts, Myths and Evidence

sources.title: Bridge Types: Tensile & Compressive Forces
notes: Explains how tension and compression act in bridge members and how bridge geometry changes the force path.
Uses simplified teaching models; real designs also depend on material properties, joints, bracing, loading and support conditions.

sources.title: Building Bridges Activity: Beam, Truss, Arch, and Suspension
sources.publisher: Center for Architecture, AIA New York
notes: Compares beam, truss, arch and suspension bridge concepts and uses structural-force illustrations to explain their behaviour.
An educational activity that clarifies mechanisms rather than specifying engineering design capacity.

sources.title: The Types of Bridges
notes: Explains arch thrust, compression-dominated action and the way bridge forms span openings.
Treats bridge forms as distinct force systems; dimensions and site conditions determine real capacity.

sources.title: Load Rating
notes: Describes bridge load rating as an engineering evaluation of existing structures against defined loads and assumptions.
The rating framework supports decisions on capacity and restrictions; it should not be interpreted as a universal safe weight for every situation.

sources.title: Introduction to the Different Types of Bridges
notes: Provides teaching material on bridge types, including permanent and changing loads and the role of foundations and supports.
Conceptual teaching examples illustrate force transfer; site-specific analysis is needed for actual design.
